units.title: Actual Gaussian TV amplification (Ex72)
units.reader_note: The main bound is shown first; actual laws, source assumptions, proof steps and exact Lean are folded below.
units.statement: The total variation distance between the actual averaged Gaussian targets has the following explicit lower bound.
assumptions: \(d,n\in\mathbb N,\ 3\le n\le d,\ \kappa\ge4\); set \(k=\lfloor d/n\rfloor\) and \(r=d-kn=d\bmod n\). Both endpoint inequalities are inclusive.

For normalized full orthogonal Haar probability \(\mu_n\), let \(\nu_\pm=2\mu_n|_{\{\det O=\pm1\}}\). Define \(A_O=\frac{\kappa+1}{2}I-\frac{\kappa-1}{4}(O+O^\top)\), \(\mathcal D_\pm=(\boldsymbol O\mapsto\operatorname{diag}(A_{O_1},\ldots,A_{O_k},I_r))_\#\nu_\pm^{\otimes k}\), and the actual averaged targets \(\bar\pi_\pm=\int\mathcal N(0,A^{-1})\,d\mathcal D_\pm(A)\). Each product uses one common sign.

Total variation uses the source probability convention \(\delta=\sup_{B\text{ measurable}}|\bar\pi_+(B)-\bar\pi_-(B)|=\frac12\int|f-g|\,dx\). In Lean, each event mass is \(M_\pm.\mathrm{real}(B)=\operatorname{toReal}(M_\pm(B))\); the actual laws are proved to be probabilities internally, so all event masses are finite. Nonempty/bounded event-supremum and mass-one density obligations are discharged by the canonical normalized-density theorem.

The proof uses actual ambient RN densities \(f=d\bar\pi_+/dx\), \(g=d\bar\pi_-/dx\), and actual block affinity \(a=\int\sqrt{p_+p_-}\). Absolute continuity, L1, normalization, the exact tensorization \(\int\sqrt{fg}=a^k\), and Eq25 are derived from existing canonical producers. They are not supplied as additional hypotheses.

The residual factor is included for \(r>0\); for \(r=0\), it is the zero-dimensional unit factor from the existing actual product-law and affinity producers. The theorem imposes no positive-remainder condition and includes all source-domain endpoints.

notation.text: TV is the supremum of actual probability differences over measurable events. Natural division selects the number of full common-sign blocks.

steps.title: Establish probability and actual RN densities
steps.text: The existing actual averaged block-law theorem supplies probability for both full-dimensional Gaussian binds. The actual affinity theorem supplies absolute continuity. RN integration for finite measures over sigma-finite Euclidean volume then gives nonnegative measurable genuine L1 densities of unit mass, with no infinite-value real-conversion shortcut.
steps.lean: hp/hm consume AveragedBlockLaw.actual_averaged_block_product. ht consumes AffinityTensorization.actual_affinity_tensorization. hfi/hgi and hf1/hg1 use Measure.integrable_toReal_rnDeriv and Measure.integral_toReal_rnDeriv with actual probability instances.

steps.title: Identify the exact event TV
steps.text: For every measurable event, the integral of its RN density equals the actual law probability. This identifies the source event supremum with the same event supremum in the canonical normalized-density comparison. That theorem proves nonemptiness, boundedness and the exact factor one half; the totalized supremum is not used without its valid domain.
steps.lean: hset is equality of the two actual event-discrepancy sets, using Measure.setIntegral_toReal_rnDeriv for both AC laws. hc is the same canonical DensityAffinity.normalized_density_tv_affinity node already used by earlier packets.

steps.title: Apply the overlap–affinity comparison
steps.text: The source writes TV as one minus overlap and bounds min(f,g) by sqrt(fg). The shared density theorem proves the equivalent pointwise inequality f+g-2sqrt(fg)<=|f-g|, integrates genuine L1 functions and uses their unit masses and the exact half-L1 TV identity. It therefore gives the same lower comparison for these actual laws. The displayed overlap formula explains this equivalence; no separate newly exported min-integral identity is claimed.
steps.lean: hc.2.2.2.2.1 and hset give htv. The canonical producer proves the pointwise comparison by cases f<=g, followed by integral_mono and normalization. This is an explicit equivalent algebraic route to the source overlap comparison.

steps.title: Use actual tensorization and the single-block bound
steps.text: The actual affinity theorem identifies the ambient affinity with a^k, including zero residual dimension. Eq25 controls that same actual block affinity. Nonnegativity allows monotonicity of natural powers; the exponential power identity gives the exact coefficient and sign in the source bound.
steps.lean: ht.2.2.2 is the actual Ex71 equality. hb is SingleBlockAffinity.single_block_affinity_bound; ha composes its final two inequalities. hpow uses pow_le_pow_left₀, Real.exp_nat_mul and ring.

steps.title: Conclude actual TV separation
steps.text: Subtract the affinity upper bound from one and combine it with the actual-TV lower comparison. The focused consumer shows that an explicit block-count/condition-number threshold makes the actual law TV at least one half; it is not a statement about a scalar substitute or about query costs.
steps.lean: The final rw substitutes ht.2.2.2 into htv, then sub_le_sub_left hpow 1 and trans close the sealed theorem. Tests.GaussianComplexityTVAmplification is the actual-law fixed-accuracy consumer.

units.lean_statement: Exactly the preproof sealed final-Ex72 inequality. Source bounds 3<=n<=d and kappa>=4 are the only logical premises.
units.lean_proof: The exact complete production theorem is extracted beside the proof; all mathematical ingredients are canonical dependencies or internal proofs.
units.boundary: Selected final Ex72 inequality for the actual averaged Gaussian laws, plus a focused actual-TV>=1/2 consumer under the explicit parameter threshold k*exp(-10n/sqrt(kappa))/8>=log 2. No oracle/transcript, exact-matvec query lower bound, deterministic worst-case cap, sampling-TV-precision reduction, expected-cost adapter or fixed-spectrum hidden-eigenbasis lower bound is asserted here. Independent source verification, root/site integration, remote publication, postmerge purification/Exposition Seal and whole Goal completion are separate phases.
